items.explanation: が marks 日本語のガイド as the thing whose existence is asked about; it is the subject of the pattern 〜があります.

items.jp: 二、三デメリットがありますね。

translation.pt-BR: Há duas ou três desvantagens, né.
translation.en: There are a few disadvantages to it.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks デメリット as the thing whose existence is asserted; it is the subject of the pattern 〜があります.

items.jp: 道が２つの小道に分かれるところへ来た。

translation.pt-BR: Chegamos a um ponto onde a estrada se dividia em duas trilhas.
translation.en: We came to a place where the road branched into two lanes.

items.label: subject marker (within the relative clause)
items.explanation: が marks 道 ('the road') as the subject of the clause that describes ところ; within relative clauses が is common.
tokens: destination (head modified by the relative clause)

items.jp: 天気がよければハイキングに行くのだが。

translation.pt-BR: Se o tempo estivesse bom, a gente iria fazer uma trilha...
translation.en: Were it clear, we would go on a hike.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が marks 天気 ('the weather') as the subject of the condition ('if the weather is good'); within a subordinate clause the subject usually takes が, not は.

items.jp: りんごがほしい?

translation.pt-BR: Você quer uma maçã?
translation.en: Do you want an apple?

items.label: marks the object of desire
items.explanation: in the pattern 〜がほしい, the thing one desires is marked by が (not を), because ほしい is a stative adjective. That's why りんご takes が.

items.jp: りんごがほしいですか？

translation.pt-BR: Você quer maçã?
translation.en: Do you want an apple?

items.label: marker of the desired object
items.explanation: が marks りんご ('apple') as that which is desired, within the pattern 〜がほしい.

items.jp: 千人くらいの人がいた。

translation.pt-BR: Havia cerca de mil pessoas.
translation.en: There were toward a thousand people.

items.label: marks the subject of existence
items.explanation: が points to who 'existed/there was'. With existence verbs like いる, a newly introduced subject is usually marked by が, not は.
tokens: counter suffix (form 千人 = 'a thousand people')

items.jp: 人気があるんですか？

translation.pt-BR: É popular?
translation.en: Is it popular?

items.label: subject particle (が)
items.explanation: It marks 人気 as the thing that 'exists'; in 〜がある, が points to what possesses the existence ('there is popularity').
tokens: main verb (forms the expression 人気がある = 'to be popular')

items.jp: それより、本を読んだほうがいい。

translation.pt-BR: Em vez disso, é melhor você ler livros.
translation.en: You ought to read books instead.

items.label: subject particle (in the pattern 〜ほうがいい)
items.explanation: Marks ほう as the element that 'is good', the core of the recommendation 〜ほうがいい.

items.jp: 車の中に何本かのペンがありますか。

translation.pt-BR: Tem algumas canetas dentro do carro?
translation.en: Are there any pens in the car?

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 何本かのペン as the thing whose existence is asked about; it is the subject of the pattern 〜があります.

items.jp: 車がほしいですか。

translation.pt-BR: Você quer um carro?
translation.en: Do you want a car?

items.label: marker of the desired object
items.explanation: in the pattern 〜がほしい, the thing one wants takes が (not を), because ほしい is an adjective and treats the desired item as the grammatical subject.

items.jp: ２０分ごとにバスがある。

translation.pt-BR: Há um ônibus a cada 20 minutos.
translation.en: There is a bus every 20 minutes.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks バス ('bus') as the subject that 'exists', presenting new information (there is a bus...).

items.jp: 魚がいいのですが。

translation.pt-BR: Eu gostaria de peixe, se possível.
translation.en: I'd like some fish.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 魚 ('fish') as that which 'is good/preferable'; with いい, が is used to indicate the object of the preference.

items.jp: ごめんなさい。時間があまりないんです。

translation.pt-BR: Desculpe. É que não tenho muito tempo.
translation.en: I'm sorry. I don't have a lot of time.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 時間 (time) as the subject whose existence is denied by ない (I have no time).
tokens: adverb (paired with the negation ない)
auxiliary (polite copula, part of んです)

items.jp: 何か食べるものがほしい。

translation.pt-BR: Quero algo para comer.
translation.en: I want something to eat.

items.label: marker of the desired object
items.explanation: が marks the block 食べるもの ('something to eat') as that which is desired, according to 〜がほしい.
tokens: verb that modifies the following noun

items.jp: どちらがあなたのギターですか。

translation.pt-BR: Qual é o seu violão?
translation.en: Which is your guitar?

items.label: subject/focus marker
items.explanation: が marks どちら as the focus of the question ('WHICH is...'); interrogative pronouns use が, not は.
tokens: interrogative pronoun / focus of the question

items.jp: さっさと行ったほうがいい。

translation.pt-BR: É melhor a gente ir logo.
translation.en: We'd better get a move on.

items.label: subject marker (within the ほうがいい pattern)
items.explanation: が links ほう to いい in the fixed pattern ほうがいい: 'the side (of going right away) is good', that is, 'it's better to go'.
tokens: noun of the ほうがいい pattern ("that option")

items.jp: ここにいくつかのバッグがあります。

translation.pt-BR: Aqui há algumas bolsas.
translation.en: We have several bags here.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が marks 'バッグ' as the subject that exists; with あります, が (not は) is used to introduce something new in the scene.

items.jp: ウスターソースがいいんじゃない？

translation.pt-BR: Que tal molho inglês? Acho que fica bom.
translation.en: How about adding some Worcestershire sauce?

items.label: subject particle (focus)
items.explanation: が presents ウスターソース as that which 'would be good', highlighting it as the option in focus in the suggestion.

items.jp: ちょっと話があるんだけど。

translation.pt-BR: Preciso falar uma coisa com você...
translation.en: I need to talk to you.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が marks 話 as the thing that 'exists'; with ある, が is used to point to what there is ('there is a matter').

items.jp: もっと休みをとったほうがいい。

translation.pt-BR: É melhor você descansar mais.
translation.en: I think you should get more rest.

items.label: marks the subject of いい within ～ほうがいい
items.explanation: が points to ほう ('the option of taking more rest') as that which 'is better'; it is the fixed が of the ～たほうがいい pattern.

items.jp: 少し休んだほうがいい。

translation.pt-BR: É melhor você descansar um pouco.
translation.en: You should get some rest.

items.label: subject particle within the pattern
items.explanation: が marks ほう as that which 'is good'; it is the fixed particle of the 〜ほうがいい pattern, highlighting the advised option (to rest).
tokens: head of the 〜ほうがいい pattern

items.jp: 時間があるか分かりません。

translation.pt-BR: Não sei se vou ter tempo.
translation.en: I don't know if I have the time.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 時間 as that which 'exists'; with verbs like ある/いる, the subject takes が, not は.

items.jp: それがどこから来たのか分からなかった。

translation.pt-BR: Eu não sabia de onde aquilo tinha vindo.
translation.en: I didn't know where it came from.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks それ ('that') as the subject of what was not known (the focus of the new information).

items.jp: 時間があるかどうか分からない。

translation.pt-BR: Não sei se vou ter tempo.
translation.en: I don't know if I'll have time.

items.label: subject particle (が)
items.explanation: が marks 時間 as the subject of the verb ある within the embedded clause ('time exists / I have time').
tokens: fixed element of the expression かどうか

items.jp: 目が口よりものを言う時がある。

translation.pt-BR: Às vezes os olhos falam mais do que a boca.
translation.en: Eyes sometimes talk louder than words.

items.label: particle が: marks the subject (目, the eyes)
items.explanation: が highlights 目 as the subject performing the action 言う; here it presents the eyes as the element in focus in the comparison.
tokens: object of comparison (pattern marked by より)

items.jp: 目が口よりものを言う時がある。

translation.pt-BR: Às vezes os olhos falam mais do que a boca.
translation.en: Eyes sometimes talk louder than words.

items.label: particle が: marks the subject of ある (時)
items.explanation: が here marks 時 as the subject of the existence verb ある, forming the expression 時がある = 'there are times (when)'.
tokens: object of comparison (pattern marked by より)

items.jp: 木の下にベンチがあります。

translation.pt-BR: Tem um banco embaixo da árvore.
translation.en: There is a bench under the tree.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が points to ベンチ as the thing whose existence is being asserted; it is the obligatory subject of the pattern 〜があります.

items.jp: いい人だけどイマイチね。

translation.pt-BR: Ele é uma boa pessoa, mas falta alguma coisa.
translation.en: He is nice, but he's not the one for me.

items.label: contrastive connector ('but')
items.explanation: けど (here in だ+けど = だけど) links the two clauses in opposition: 'is a good person, BUT something is lacking'. It is the focus of the sentence, more colloquial than が.

items.jp: すしって何ですか

translation.pt-BR: O que é sushi?
translation.en: What is sushi?

items.label: colloquial topic (= は / というのは)
items.explanation: って presents すし as the topic being asked about; it is the spoken form of 'as for sushi' when requesting a definition.

items.jp: １３って言った？それとも３０？

translation.pt-BR: Você disse 13? Ou foi 30?
translation.en: Did you say 13 or 30?

items.label: informal quotation marker
items.explanation: って quotes in a colloquial way what was said ("13") before the verb 言った, equivalent to the formal と言った.

items.jp: 三時ごろに駅で会おう

translation.pt-BR: Vamos nos encontrar na estação lá pelas três horas.
translation.en: Let's meet at the station around three o'clock.

items.label: marker of the place where the action occurs
items.explanation: で indicates the place where the meeting happens (the station), characteristic of で for the setting of an active action, unlike the に of mere existence.

items.jp: 名前を書くだけでいいです

translation.pt-BR: Basta escrever o nome.
translation.en: You just have to write your name.

items.label: marker of means/sufficient condition
items.explanation: で here forms the set 〜だけで, presenting this single action as the sufficient means for the result いい ('that's all it takes').

items.jp: 左手で書いてみようとした。

translation.pt-BR: Eu tentei escrever com a mão esquerda.
translation.en: I tried to write with my left hand.

items.label: particle of means/instrument
items.explanation: で marks 左手 as the instrument used for the action of writing.
tokens: main verb of the attempted action
auxiliary verb (〜てみる) in volitional form
verb (auxiliary of the 〜うとした pattern)

items.jp: また後で。

translation.pt-BR: Até mais tarde.
translation.en: I'll see you later.

items.label: temporal/locative particle forming the expression 後で
items.explanation: で here marks the moment when something will occur ('in/after some time later'); fused with 後 it becomes the fixed expression 後で = 'later, afterward', the temporal point of the farewell.

items.jp: お水だけでけっこうです。

translation.pt-BR: Só água está bom, por favor.
translation.en: Just water, please.

items.label: indicates means/condition: 'with this, this being so'
items.explanation: で here presents お水だけ as what suffices: 'with just water (it's fine)'.

items.jp: ここで会えてよかった。

translation.pt-BR: Que bom poder te encontrar aqui.
translation.en: I'm glad to see you here.

items.label: marks the place where the action occurs
items.explanation: で indicates the place of a concrete action (meeting happens 'here'), unlike に, which would mark mere existence/position.

items.jp: ともだちと コーヒーを のむ

translation.pt-BR: Eu tomo café com um amigo.
translation.en: I have coffee with a friend.

items.label: companionship particle
items.explanation: と marks ともだち ('friend') as the person with whom the action is carried out (having coffee together).

items.jp: 見てみたいな。

translation.pt-BR: Queria ver isso.
translation.en: I want to see them.

items.label: sentence-final particle of feeling
items.explanation: な at the end softens and expresses the speaker's emotion/desire, giving the tone of 'ah, I'd like to see that...'.

items.jp: 何か飲みたいな。

translation.pt-BR: Queria beber alguma coisa.
translation.en: I want to drink something.

items.label: sentence-final particle of feeling
items.explanation: な at the end expresses the speaker's desire/venting, giving the tone of 'I'd like to drink something...'.

items.jp: 本を買いに本やにいきました

translation.pt-BR: Fui à livraria comprar um livro.
translation.en: I went to the bookstore to buy a book.

items.label: purpose particle
items.explanation: this first に, right after the stem 買い, expresses the purpose of the movement: 'in order to buy'. It is the pattern 〜にいく. (The second に, before いきました, is different: it marks the destination 本や 'to the bookstore'.)

items.jp: ひるごはんを食べにいきます

translation.pt-BR: Vou almoçar.
translation.en: I'm going to have lunch.

items.label: purpose particle
items.explanation: に after the stem 食べ links the action 'to eat' to the movement verb いきます, indicating the purpose of going: 'to go in order to eat'.

items.jp: 電車でもバスでも駅に行ける

translation.pt-BR: Dá pra chegar na estação tanto de trem quanto de ônibus.
translation.en: You can get to the station either by train or by bus.

items.label: direction/destination particle
items.explanation: に marks 駅 as the arrival point of the movement verb 行ける ('to be able to go to the station').

items.jp: 誰とえいがを見にいきますか

translation.pt-BR: Com quem você vai ao cinema?
translation.en: Who are you going to the movies with?

items.label: purpose particle
items.explanation: に after the verb stem (見) indicates the purpose of the movement: 'to go to watch' (go and watch).

items.jp: 道が２つの小道に分かれるところへ来た。

translation.pt-BR: Chegamos a um ponto onde a estrada se dividia em duas trilhas.
translation.en: We came to a place where the road branched into two lanes.

items.label: marks the result/of the division
items.explanation: に indicates the result of 分かれる: the road splits 'into' two paths.
tokens: destination (head modified by the relative clause)

items.jp: パンを買いにいく。

translation.pt-BR: Vou comprar pão.
translation.en: I'll go buy some bread.

items.label: marks the purpose of the movement
items.explanation: に after the stem 買い forms '買いに行く' = 'go to buy'. Here に links the purpose-action to the verb 行く (the purpose pattern 〜に行く).

items.jp: 外に出ようとしない。

translation.pt-BR: Ele não dá sinal de querer sair.
translation.en: He would not go out.

items.label: destination/direction marker
items.explanation: に indicates the target point of the movement of 出る: to go out to 外 (outside).

items.jp: 見たいのかしら？

translation.pt-BR: Será que ele quer ver?
translation.en: Does he want to see it?

items.label: nominalizer / explanatory tone
items.explanation: の turns 見たい into something nominalized and gives the nuance of 'it's that (he) wants to see', setting up the internal question that comes with かしら.

items.jp: どこから来たのか。

translation.pt-BR: De onde você veio?
translation.en: Where did you come from?

items.label: nominalizer / explanatory particle の
items.explanation: This の turns the sentence into something like 'the fact of having come', giving a tone of explanation or of a question about the circumstance (the の nominalizer).

items.jp: それがどこから来たのか分からなかった。

translation.pt-BR: Eu não sabia de onde aquilo tinha vindo.
translation.en: I didn't know where it came from.

items.label: nominalizing particle (準体助詞)
items.explanation: の nominalizes the clause 来た, turning 'came' into something like 'the fact of having come', setting up the indirect question.

items.jp: どれくらいかかるのかしら。

translation.pt-BR: Quanto tempo será que vai levar?
translation.en: I wonder how long it's going to take.

items.label: nominalizer / explanatory-interrogative particle
items.explanation: の turns the clause かかる into a nominal block and gives the tone of a question with an explanatory nuance ('just how much it takes...'), setting up the doubt expressed by かしら.

items.jp: あれ？あなたまだここにいたのね！

translation.pt-BR: Ué? Você ainda estava aqui, hein!
translation.en: Huh? You were still here?!

items.label: nominalizing/explanatory particle (の of のね)
items.explanation: の here gives an explanatory/observational tone ('the thing is...'), setting up the sentence for the tone of surprise at the final のね.

items.jp: あれ？何だろ？パフォーマンスでもやってるのか？

translation.pt-BR: Hã? O que é isso? Será que estão fazendo uma apresentação de rua ou algo assim?
translation.en: Hello, what's that? Somebody doing street theatre or something?

items.label: nominalizes the clause and gives an explanatory/dubitative tone
items.explanation: This 「の」 turns 「やってる」 into something like 'the fact that they're doing it', setting up the question with the sense of 'I wonder if...'.

items.jp: なんで学校を休んだの

translation.pt-BR: Por que você faltou à escola?
translation.en: Why did you miss school?

items.label: sentence-final question particle (casual)
items.explanation: の ends the sentence as a question with an informal, curious tone, common when questioning someone close.

items.jp: きのうなんで来なかったの

translation.pt-BR: Por que você não veio ontem?
translation.en: Why didn't you come yesterday?

items.label: sentence-final question particle (casual)
items.explanation: の turns the sentence into a question with a close, informal tone, common when amicably calling out someone's absence.

items.jp: とにかく行きたくなかったの。

translation.pt-BR: De qualquer forma, eu não queria ir lá.
translation.en: I didn't want to go there anyway.

items.label: explanatory/softening sentence-final particle
items.explanation: の at the end of the sentence gives a tone of explanation or confidence ('it's that...', 'you know'), making the remark more personal and gentle.

items.jp: 見せたいところがあるの。

translation.pt-BR: Tem um lugar que eu quero te mostrar.
translation.en: There's a place I'd like to show you.

items.label: explanatory sentence-final particle
items.explanation: の (=んです informal) gives an explanatory/soft tone, typical of colloquial speech.

items.jp: 今日は休めと言われたんだけど。

translation.pt-BR: É que me disseram para eu folgar hoje...
translation.en: He said that I shouldn't even be coming in today.

items.label: topic marker
items.explanation: は marks 今日 (today) as the topic of the sentence, with a slight contrast relative to other days.
tokens: auxiliary (copula of the explanatory structure んだ)

items.jp: レモンはすっぱいくだものだ。

translation.pt-BR: O limão é uma fruta azeda.
translation.en: The lemon is a sour fruit.

items.label: topic marker
items.explanation: は presents レモン as the theme of the sentence: 'speaking of lemons...'. It is the standard topic marker in generalizing statements.

items.jp: この川は何というのですか。

translation.pt-BR: Como se chama este rio?
translation.en: What is the name of this river?

items.label: topic marker
items.explanation: は marks この川 as the theme of the question: 'speaking of this river'.
tokens: verb (part of the 何という pattern)

items.jp: 母は毎日うちにいます。

translation.pt-BR: Minha mãe fica em casa todos os dias.
translation.en: Mother stays at home every day.

items.label: topic particle (whom one is talking about)
items.explanation: Marks 母 as the topic of the sentence: 'as for mother...'; introduces the subject before describing what she does.

items.jp: 母は先週インフルエンザにかかりました。

translation.pt-BR: Minha mãe pegou gripe semana passada.
translation.en: Last week my mother came down with the flu.

items.label: topic marker
items.explanation: は apresenta 母 como o tema da frase: é sobre a mãe que se vai contar alguma coisa.

items.jp: 父はついさきほど出かけた。

translation.pt-BR: Meu pai saiu agorinha mesmo.
translation.en: My father went out just now.

items.label: marks the topic of the sentence
items.explanation: は presents 父 as the subject of the sentence ('as for my father...').

items.jp: バスはちょうど出たところだった。

translation.pt-BR: O ônibus tinha acabado de sair.
translation.en: The bus has just left.

items.label: topic marker
items.explanation: は introduces バス as the topic/subject about which it is commented that it has just left.
tokens: formal noun of the たところ pattern

items.jp: 駅まで二キロメートルあります

translation.pt-BR: Daqui até a estação são dois quilômetros.
translation.en: It's two kilometers from here to the station.

items.label: limit/extent particle ('until')
items.explanation: まで marks 駅 as the point up to which the distance extends: 'up to the station'. It indicates the destination/limit of the measured route.

items.jp: ここから学校まで三キロくらいだ

translation.pt-BR: Daqui até a escola são uns três quilômetros.
translation.en: From here to the school is about three kilometers.

items.label: limit/destination particle
items.explanation: まで marks 学校 (school) as the end of the stretch; together with から it defines the measured route.

items.jp: どうもありがとうございました

translation.pt-BR: Muito obrigado mesmo.
translation.en: Thank you so much, really.

items.label: emphasis/addition particle
items.explanation: Here も is fixed within the expression どうも; historically it reinforces どう, giving the sense of 'really, very'. In practice, どうも is treated as a single word of emphasis.

items.jp: そして何時間もいっしょに話したからです。

translation.pt-BR: E porque conversamos juntos por horas a fio.
translation.en: And we had spent hours talking together.

items.label: emphasis particle (quantity)
items.explanation: も after 何時間 emphasizes that it was a long time, giving the sense of 'hours and hours / for several hours'.

items.jp: おくびにも出すな。

translation.pt-BR: Não conte isso a ninguém.
translation.en: Don't breathe a word of it to anyone.

items.label: emphasis particle 'not even'
items.explanation: も here reinforces 'not even': not even by a burp, that is, by no means let it show.

items.jp: あの男ももう上がったりだ。

translation.pt-BR: Aquele cara também já era.
translation.en: He is done for.

items.label: も of inclusion ('also')
items.explanation: も marks あの男 as one more case, suggesting that, like others, this guy too is done for.

items.jp: 電気つけっぱなしだよ。

translation.pt-BR: Você deixou a luz acesa, viu.
translation.en: You left the lights on.

items.label: sentence-final particle (emphasis/warning)
items.explanation: よ adds a tone of warning to the listener, drawing attention to the fact that the light was left on.

items.jp: びびってなんかないよ。

translation.pt-BR: Eu não tô com medo, viu.
translation.en: I'm not chicken.

items.label: sentence-final particle よ (assertion directed at the listener)
items.explanation: Reinforces the statement, making clear to the listener that they are mistaken ('I'm not scared, you know').
tokens: component of the emphatic なんか

items.jp: 電車よりバスのほうが安いです

translation.pt-BR: O ônibus é mais barato que o trem.
translation.en: The bus is cheaper than the train.

items.explanation: より marks 電車 as the reference point of the comparison ('cheaper than the train').
tokens: noun (term of comparison, the reference point)
formal noun of the 〜のほうが structure

items.jp: この店のほうがあの店より安い

translation.pt-BR: Esta loja é mais barata que aquela.
translation.en: This store is cheaper than that one.

items.label: marks the point of comparison ('than that store')
items.explanation: より means 'compared to / than'. It attaches to あの店 to say that the comparison is made in relation to that store.
tokens: first term of the comparison (the 'more' side)
head of the 〜のほうが pattern
determiner (連体詞) accompanying the second 店
second term of the comparison (the reference point)

items.jp: それより、本を読んだほうがいい。

translation.pt-BR: Em vez disso, é melhor você ler livros.
translation.en: You ought to read books instead.

items.label: comparison particle (than)
